description: The figure contains three side-by-side grouped bar charts labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4, illustrating model perplexity as a function of quantization bit-width for two methods (“Uniform” and “Ours”). In each subplot, the horizontal axis lists the category “Quantization Bits” with four discrete values (3, 4, 8, 16) in increasing order, and the vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” on a linear scale; in (a) the plotted range is roughly 0 to a little above 30 with ticks at regular small intervals, in (b) the range extends from 0 to a little above 400 with ticks spaced by about 50, and in (c) the range is roughly 0 to a little above 30 with ticks at regular small intervals. Each quantization-bit category contains two adjacent bars: a blue bar for “Uniform” and an orange bar for “Ours,” as indicated by the legend in the upper-left of each subplot. In (a) WikiText, the blue “Uniform” bars are approximately 31 at 3 bits, ~27 at 4 bits, and ~26.5 at both 8 and 16 bits, while the orange “Ours” bars are approximately ~21.5 at 3 bits, ~19 at 4 bits, and ~18.3 at both 8 and 16 bits. In (b) PTB, the blue “Uniform” bars are approximately ~420 at 3 bits, ~315 at 4 bits, and ~298–300 at both 8 and 16 bits, while the orange “Ours” bars are approximately ~245 at 3 bits, ~178 at 4 bits, and ~182–183 at both 8 and 16 bits. In (c) C4, the blue “Uniform” bars are approximately ~29 at 3 bits, ~25 at 4 bits, and ~24.5 at both 8 and 16 bits, while the orange “Ours” bars are approximately ~20.5 at 3 bits, ~18.1 at 4 bits, and ~17.7–17.8 at both 8 and 16 bits. The bars are not visually emphasized beyond consistent coloring and grouping, and there are no annotations or error bars; categories appear ordered by increasing bit-width rather than sorted by bar height.
